purpose: One development run rehearsing Chapter 3 (Objectives 1, 3 and 4) on the released 16-interval grid and on a 32-interval grid with the paper's stopping rule, with the paper's 14 + 2 setting, teacher-only and student-only

outputs.s025: 32-interval s = 0.25 (14 teacher steps), reference on this grid

grid32: t_i = 1 - cos(pi/2 * i/32), i = 0..32; teacher to k* = max{i : t_i <= s} (Li et al., Algorithm 2)
handover: teacher endpoint estimate re-noised at the released student's levels: j = 1 for every output except 'paper' (j = 2), 'alg2' (from the teacher's state), 'teacher32' (no student) and 'student4' (four student steps from noise); guidance gamma = 2, no stochastic term; same seeds
objective1: per candidate: WER, SIM, UTMOS, added-failure rate with Clopper-Pearson 95% intervals, per condition; oracle (cheapest non-failing candidate) per condition and its share earlier than the reference; Spearman correlation of the prompt SNR and of the drift at each candidate with the oracle's candidate index; SNR gate = lowest value in 20.0..40.0 dB above which the earliest candidate fails at most 5%

schedulers.later5: SNR gate (20 dB), fixed later step 5
schedulers.later6: SNR gate (20 dB), fixed later step 6
schedulers.snr_drift_dev: Full policy, gate from the Objective 1 rule
schedulers.oracle: Oracle: cheapest safe candidate in hindsight (diagnostic)

calibration: fixed-sequence Learn-Then-Test (Algorithm 3.4), pooled binomial p-value, alpha 0.05, delta 0.1
objective3: 100 random 80/20 speaker re-splits; calibration sizes [50, 100, 200] cases; certified share, test risk, saving
objective4: every method of Table 3 (compared methods) plus SNR + TAS: failures with exact intervals, mean forward passes, saving and share of the oracle saving with 1000 speaker bootstrap resamples, runtime and real-time factor, worst-condition rate; Wilcoxon signed-rank on speaker-level differences with Holm correction; exact McNemar (full policy against SNR-only, the fixed-later-step controls, stabilization only and the cost-matched random rule); TOST equivalence with margins {'wer': 0.01, 'similarity': 0.02}; robustness: calibrate on clean prompts, test on noisy prompts
random_rule: per input, the reference with probability p, else a uniformly random early candidate; p matches the full policy's mean cost; 100 seeded draws
tas: one-sided squared Mahalanobis distance of log(d_1..d_k) from the clean training prompts; k = 4 (16-interval), 7 (32-interval)
